spots.name: Potemkin Stairs
spots.summary: The Potemkin Stairs, Potemkin Steps, or officially, the Prymorski Stairs, are a giant stairway in Odesa, Ukraine. They are considered a formal entrance into the city from the direction of the sea and are the best known symbol of Odesa.

spots.name: Historic Centre of Odesa
spots.summary: The Historic Centre of Odesa, Historical City Centre of Odesa, or Centre of Odesa is a city centre and World Heritage Site in Odesa, Ukraine. It was listed in 2023, and currently, it is on the list of World Heritage Sites in Danger because of the Russo-Ukrainian war.

Transfiguration Cathedral

spots.summary: The Transfiguration Cathedral is the Orthodox Cathedral in Odesa, Ukraine, dedicated to the Transfiguration of Jesus and belongs to the Ukrainian Orthodox Church.

spots.name: Odesa Opera and Ballet Theatre

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Odesa National Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre is the oldest theatre in Odesa, Ukraine. The Theatre and the Potemkin Stairs are the most famous edifices in Odesa.

spots.name: Khadjibey

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Khadjibey was a fortress and a haven by the Gulf of Odesa, in the location of the modern city of Odesa, Ukraine. The settlement was destroyed and abandoned in the 15th or 16th century and was revived under the Ottoman Empire in the 18th century.

spots.name: Monument to the founders of Odesa
spots.summary: Monument to the founders of Odesa, also known as the monument to Empress Catherine II of Russia and her companions, was a monument located in Odesa, Ukraine, on then Katerynska Square.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monument to the founders of Odesa

spots.name: Derybasivska Street
spots.summary: Vulytsia Derybasivska or De Ribas Street is a pedestrian walkway (street) in the heart of Odesa, Ukraine. The street is named after José de Ribas, who was the builder of Odesa, the head of military and civil administration and had a house on this street.

spots.name: Vorontsov Lighthouse
spots.summary: The Vorontsov Lighthouse is a red-and-white, 27.2-metre-tall (89 ft) lighthouse in the Black Sea port of Odesa, Ukraine. It is named after Prince Mikhail Semyonovich Vorontsov, one of the governors-general of the Odesa region.

spots.name: Prymorskyi Boulevard
spots.summary: Prymorskyi Boulevard, also known by its Russian-language name as Primorsky Boulevard is a street located in the Historic Centre of Odesa, Ukraine.

spots.name: Odesa Archaeological Museum
spots.summary: The Odesa Archaeological Museum is one of the oldest archaeological museums in Ukraine. It was founded in 1825; the current museum building was completed in 1883 according to a design by Polish architect Feliks Gąsiorowski.

spots.name: Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary Cathedral, Odesa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary Cathedral also called Cathedral of the Blessed Virgin Mary is the name given to a religious building belonging to the Catholic Church and is located in the city of Odesa in the southwest part of the European country of Ukraine.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary Cathedral, Odesa

spots.name: Odesa Zoo
spots.summary: The Odesa Zoo has the status of a nature reserve of nationwide value, which was granted in 1992. The collection of the zoo is about 1,600 animals, a part from which are mentioned in International Red Book, red book of Ukraine and European Red List.

spots.name: St. Paul Cathedral

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Built in 1824, reopened in 1897. Accommodates up to 1,200. The new cathedral promises to be a much needed centre for Odesa’s Lutheran and German communities.

spots.name: Vorontsov Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Vorontsov Palace is a 19th-century palace and colonnade in Odesa, Ukraine, at the end of the Prymorskyi Boulevard pedestrian walkway.

spots.name: Odesa Museum of Western and Eastern Art

hours.note: Closed Wed

spots.summary: The Odesa Museum of Western and Eastern Art is a museum of Fine Arts on Italiiska street in Odesa, Ukraine.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Odesa Museum of Western and Eastern Art

spots.name: Odesa city garden
spots.summary: The Odesa City garden is located in town centre of Odesa, Ukraine, at the Derybasivska Street. Founded by Felix de Ribas in 1803, it is the oldest park in the city.

spots.name: Al-Salam Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Al-Salam Mosque and Arabian Cultural Center are located in Odesa, Ukraine. The cultural center and mosque were opened in June 2001.

spots.name: Odesa City Hall

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Odesa City Hall is the city hall of Odesa, Ukraine, located at the junction of Prymorskyi Boulevard, Teatralnyi Lane and Italiiska Street. It occupies a Neoclassical building, built to a design by Francesco Boffo and Gregorio Toricelli in 1828–34. Rebuilt in 1871-1873 by Franz Morandi.

spots.name: Italiiska Street
spots.summary: Italiiska Street is a street in the downtown of Odesa, Ukraine. The street is named after Italy. The street was founded in 1827.

spots.name: Odesa Philharmonic Theater
spots.summary: The Odesa Philharmonic Theatre is a theater in Odesa, Ukraine. The design resembles the Doge's Palace in Venice.

spots.name: Arcadia Beach
spots.summary: Arcadia Beach is Odesa, Ukraine's most famous beach. It is located in the Arcadia quarter.

spots.name: Odesa Fine Arts Museum

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Odesa National Fine Arts Museum or Odesa National Art Museum is one of the principal art galleries of the city of Odesa in Ukraine. Founded in 1899, it occupies the Potocki Palace, itself a monument of early 19th century architecture.

spots.name: Odesa Botanical Garden
spots.summary: Odesa Botanical Garden is a botanical garden in Odesa, Ukraine. It is subordinated to Odesa University and consists of two territories: old territory and new territory.

spots.name: Monument to the Unknown Sailor
spots.summary: The Monument to the Unknown Sailor is a city memorial located at Shevchenko Park in the Southern Ukrainian city of Odesa. It is part of the park's Alley of Glory, with the graves of fallen sailors on each side. An eternal flame is burning at foot of the monument.

spots.name: Statue of Graf Vorontsov, Odesa
spots.summary: The Statue of Graf Vorontsov, Odessa, is a sculptural and former monument established in 1863 on the Sobor Square in Odesa in honor of Mikhail Semyonovich Vorontsov, Field Marshal, the General-Governor of Novorossiya Region and plenipotentiary governor of Bessarabia who was a graf until 1845, then knyaz from 1845.

spots.name: Arcadia
spots.summary: Arcadia is a historical part of Odesa, Ukraine, which is known as a famous resort. It is located in the coastal part of the city, close to the quarters of 5th and 7th stations of Velyky Fontan. The quarter was named after a mountainous district in Greece, which was known as the home of pastoral villagers.

spots.name: Hretska Ploshcha

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hretska Square, or Hretska Ploshcha is one of the main squares of Odesa. It is on the crossing of Hretska Street and Ukrainskykh Heroiv Avenue. At different times it has been called Aleksandrovskaya or Martynovskogo. This is one of the biggest squares of Odesa.

spots.summary: is closest to the city centre, located just underneath the Shevchenko Park. Reachable by tram #28, as well as by trolleybuses #2 or #3, then a short walk is needed. The dolphinarium is located nearby.

spots.name: Kulykove Pole
spots.summary: Kulykove Pole is a garden square and necropolis located in the Prymorskyi raion of Odesa, in a historical centre of the city. It is located near Odesa railway station.

spots.name: Brodsky Synagogue
spots.summary: The Brodsky Synagogue is a Reform Jewish synagogue, located at Zhukovskoho Street 18, in Odesa, Ukraine.

spots.summary: Built 1850, rebuilt in 1996. Sights: A mikvah (a pool used for ritual purification), bimah (altar). Houses the office of Odesa Region’s Chief Rabbi Shlomo Baksht. Library: offers an impressive selection of Jewish books and films, English-speaking staff.

spots.name: School of Stolyarsky
spots.summary: Stolyarsky School is a music school for musically gifted children established in 1933 in Odesa, Ukraine, by the violin pedagogue Pyotr Stolyarsky.

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Museum of Foreign Writers in Odesa, or Odesa Pushkin Museum, is a museum dedicated, among others, to the Russian poet Alexander Pushkin in Odesa, Ukraine.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of Foreign Writers in Odesa

spots.name: Shevchenko Park
spots.summary: Taras Shevchenko Park of Culture and Recreation is in the centre of Odesa. It is located in the central part of the city. It carries the name of Taras Shevchenko since 1954.

spots.name: House of Scientists
spots.summary: The House of Scientists in Odesa is a public institution established in 1923 to unite scientists from various scientific institutions and higher schools in the Odesa area. It was one of a number of Houses of Scientists established across the Soviet Union and the first established in Ukraine.

spots.name: Alexander II Column in Odesa
spots.summary: Alexander II Column, also known as Alexander's column or Monument to Alexander II of Russia, is a triumphal column located in Shevchenko Park, Odesa and is commemorated to the visit of Russian Emperor Alexander II the city of Odesa in 1875.

spots.summary: The Odesa Numismatics Museum is a currency museum in Ukraine. The museum preserves and exhibits ancient relics from the Northern Black Sea Region and Rus-Ukraine.
